newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish banks make fresh attack on Latam market.
newsitem.headline: Spanish banks make fresh attack on Latam market.

text.p: Spain's leading banks have made further important inroads into the lucrative Latin American market, with their latest buying spree providing a good source of income in the medium term, analysts said on Friday.
Banco Bilbao Vizcaya said on Thursday it had agreed to buy a 40 percent stake in Venezuela's largest bank, Banco Provincial, for $300 million.

Just hours earlier, Spain's leading bank, Banco Santander, beat other contenders in an auction for Venezuela's second largest bank, Banco de Venezuela, scooping up 90 percent of its shares for $338.4 million.
With these two investments, the two banks secured control of just under 40 percent of the Venezuelan banking sector.

But Venezuela was not the only target this week. Santander announced on Tuesday that it would take control of Colombia's eighth largest bank, Banco Comercial Antioqueno (Bancoquia), buying a 55 percent stake for $151 million.
"These acquisitions are really positive from a strategic point of view," said Javier Requena, senior analyst at broker Benito y Monjardin.
Banks hope their acquisitions will compensate for falling margins and growing competition at home.
Analysts believe the two banks secured good prices for their purchases with Santander paying 1.5 times book value for Banco de Venezuela and BBV paying 1.4 times for Provincial.
"The prices paid will ensure a very positive contribution to profits from 1998 onwards," Requena said.
But they said the benefits would not be reaped until 1998 due to reorganisation costs.
"We will probably see a restructuring of the recent acquisitions so profits will be lower in 1997 than 1996 but should significantly increase from 1998 onwards," he added.
Some analysts said of the two Venezuelan purchases, BBV had a marginally better deal.
"BBV's acquisition is a bit better, given that the price to book value ratio is smaller and Provincial is in a better position than Banco de Venezuela," an analyst at ABN-Amro said.
With such a strong footing in the Venezuelan market, the two banks should become fiercely competitive, analysts said.

"BBV and Santander will both try to gain market share agressively," said Requena, who added that BBV had already subscribed to a rights issue at Provincial which would reinforce its banking ratios and allow for a more competitive pricing stategy.
The acquisitions had a positive impact on the shares on Friday morning. Santander was trading at 7,590 pesetas, up 80, by 1220 GMT, while BBV was trading up 60 pesetas at 6,760.
However, the purchase and possible restructuring costs could soon weigh on prices, analysts said.

The buying spree, which has seen Spanish banks snapping up their counterparts in Latin America in recent months, is probably not over but further sizeable acquisitions in the near term are not expected, analysts said.
Santander's recent acquisitions have included Mexico's Banco Mexicano, Chile's Banco Osorno, Puerto Rico's BCH Puerto Rico, a credit card group in Uruguay and two Peruvian banks.
BBV, meanwhile, has secured Mexico's Probursa financial group, Peru's Banco Continental as well as operations in Colombia, Argentina, Panama and Puerto Rico.
